title: The Hamburg “Life After Cancer” Program: Development, Implementation and Evaluation of a Structured Survivorship-Program - A Hybrid Effectiveness-Implementation-Study
summary:
In Germany, around five million people live with or after a cancer diagnosis. Many survivors face physical, emotional, and social challenges once their treatment has finished. So far, follow-up care has mainly focused on medical aspects. The Hamburg “Life After Cancer” program was developed to close this gap and to improve the overall quality of life for cancer survivors in a holistic way.

This study is being carried out at the University Cancer Center Hamburg with 500 participants within the intervention cohort. The program offers support from patient navigators, a multidimensional questionnaire to screen for possible late effects, medical follow-up consultations, an interdisciplinary survivorship board, an individual survivorship plan, a handbook, as well as educational and peer-support opportunities (academy and café). The effectiveness of the program will be measured through questionnaires on quality of life and other health-related topics at three points in time (at the start, after 26 weeks, and after 52 weeks). To evaluate its impact, results will be compared with an external control group of additional 250 patients at the University Hospital Schleswig-Holstein, who will receive standard follow-up care without a special survivorship program. In addition, interviews will be conducted to explore how well the program works in everyday practice. The program is being developed, implemented, and evaluated in close collaboration with a patient advisory board made up of cancer survivors and relatives.

If effective, the program could serve as a model for structured survivorship care in Germany.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
N = 500 participants in the intervention cohort (University Cancer Center Hamburg (UCC Hamburg), University Medical Center Hamburg-Eppendorf):
- Diagnosis of a hemato-oncological disease (ICD-10 C00–C97)
- First diagnosis in adulthood (≥ 18 years)
- Completion of tumor therapy (exception: ongoing adjuvant hormone therapy)
- Residency in the Hamburg metropolitan region and ability to present at least once at the UCC Hamburg for study enrollment
- Eligible at any point of follow-up: immediately after completion of active tumor therapy, during tumor-specific follow-up (generally up to 5 years post-treatment), or during long-term follow-up (> 5 years post-treatment)

N = 250 participants in the control cohort (University Medical Center Schleswig-Holstein (UKSH), Campus Kiel):
- No Participation in a Survivorship-Program: usual care 
- Age 18–65 years at the time of study enrollment
- Diagnosis of a hemato-oncological disease (ICD-10 C00–C97)
- First diagnosis in adulthood (≥ 18 years)
- Completion of tumor therapy (exception: ongoing adjuvant hormone therapy)
- Eligible at any point of follow-up: immediately after completion of active tumor therapy, during tumor-specific follow-up (generally up to 5 years post-treatment), or during long-term follow-up (> 5 years post-treatment)
Exclusion criteria:
- Non-German-speaking individuals for whom completion of the questionnaires is not feasible
- Presence of a psychiatric disorder (e.g., psychosis, dementia) that prevents completion of the questionnaires
